summary: This note is a Snowflake-style reference page for the AS_BOOLEAN function, which casts a VARIANT value to a BOOLEAN value. It gives the syntax AS_BOOLEAN(<variant>), states that the argument must be an expression evaluating to a VARIANT containing a valid BOOLEAN value, and says the return type is BOOLEAN. A simple example shows TRUE, FALSE and NULL wrapped in TO_VARIANT being cast back to True, False and NULL. Navigation, feedback widgets and other page boilerplate are ignored.
one_line: Reference page for the AS_BOOLEAN function, which casts a VARIANT value to a BOOLEAN, with syntax, arguments, return type and an example.
key_facts: AS_BOOLEAN casts a VARIANT value to a BOOLEAN value.
The argument should be an expression that evaluates to a VARIANT that contains a valid BOOLEAN value.
The data type of the value returned by AS_BOOLEAN is BOOLEAN.
The page lists AS_BOOLEAN under the categories Semistructured Data (Cast) and Conversion/Casting, among others.
The example SELECT AS_BOOLEAN(TO_VARIANT(TRUE)) returns True.
The example SELECT AS_BOOLEAN(TO_VARIANT(FALSE)) returns False.
The example SELECT AS_BOOLEAN(TO_VARIANT(NULL)) returns NULL.
The page's table of contents lists the sections Syntax, Arguments, Returns and Examples.
The page is written in English.
